rationale: Matthew 12:40 itself sets the two events side by side with an "as ... so" frame (Greek hosper ... houtos): "For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth" (BSB). Because the New Testament text states the correspondence, the label is explicit, following conn-gen7-fire-2peter3, where 2 Peter states its own comparison with the flood. The wording also matches closely. In the Greek editions Biblehub lists, the twelve words after Matthew's opening "for as" are the same twelve words, in order, as the Septuagint of Jonah 1:17 (Swete; numbered 2:1 in Hebrew Bibles); the Greek Orthodox Church 1904 edition differs slightly and shares ten. The Pulpit Commentary calls the clause "Verbally from the LXX." In the BSB, Jonah 1:17 has "three days and three nights in the belly of the fish" and Matthew has "the great fish." The type is type_antitype rather than quotation because no citation formula introduces the words; they are built into a comparison. How "three days and three nights" fits the burial account is a named dispute in the lesson's Positions. It bears on the timing, not on whether 12:40 points to Jonah 1:17.
